Fig. 3: Kinematic link detection. The left y-axes show the local end-effector poses (green), averaged over the pose dimensions; the shaded region indicates the total standard deviation. The right y-axes show the precision determinants, where blue denotes no kinematic link between object and robot, and orange denotes a link. Dotted lines indicate skill boundaries estimated with TAPAS [2]. Panel (A): initially, neither mug nor tree is linked to the robot. Panel (B): external mug motion (À) triggers an updated prediction. Panel (C): after grasping, the mug becomes kinematically linked and follows the end-effector (À). Panel (D): the link ends after placement. Short-lived precision peaks at pre-grasp and during mug–tree alignment do not constitute kinematic links.
